cultural.vision_reason: The figurine depicts a mustachioed drummer in a wide sombrero-style hat, part of a "funeral band" scene rendered in painted pottery with aniline colors — this is a Latin American (Mexican) folk-art tradition, not Khmer dress or craft.

physical.title: figurine; model group
physical.summary: Figurine (part of funeral scene); made of pottery painted with aniline paints; in the form of drummer; hair, eyebrows, eyes, moustache and goatee painted black; skin pink; hat blue; shirt yellow; trousers purple; base violet; gold snare drum with strap over right shoulder/left hip, holds gold stick in each hand.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a papier-mâché skeleton figurine used for Day of the Dead festivities, a Mexican tradition unrelated to Khmer culture — no connection to Cambodia or Khmer craft/dress.

physical.title: figurine
physical.summary: Figurine in the form of a skeleton builder; made of papier mâché mounted on a wooden framework; wooden square base, painted brown with blue wavy line; skeleton (mounted on dowel painted brown) wearing newspaper hat, green paper waistcoat with blue pockets; holds grey papier mâché bucket full of green papier mâché cement in both hands; grey papier mâché trowel with blue handle rests on top. Stamped on bottom with maker's mark. Used in Day of the Dead Festival.
